content_html:
Bananas continue ripening after purchase and release ethylene, a natural gas that speeds ripening. To make them last longer, keep green bananas at room temperature, separate them from ethylene-sensitive produce when you do not want faster ripening, and refrigerate once they reach the stage you prefer.

Do not refrigerate very green bananas if you want normal ripening

Cold can slow ripening too much in very immature fruit. Keep green bananas on a cool counter away from strong sun and heat sources until they begin to yellow.

Separate them from other fruit when you want slower ripening

Apples, avocados, and other fruits also produce ethylene. Grouping them can help when faster ripening is desired, but for longer storage avoid concentrating those sources together in a closed bag.

Refrigerate once they are as ripe as you like

The peel can darken substantially in the refrigerator while the flesh remains usable for some time. Judge the inside by texture and smell rather than peel color alone.

Freeze overripe bananas before they go to waste

Peel and cut ripe bananas you will not eat fresh and freeze them in an appropriate container. They work well later in smoothies or baking, but fruit with mold or an abnormal odor should be discarded.
